title: Squared-Degree Extremality for Uniform Hypergraphs
summary: For k above half of N, the source conjectures that the complete uniform hypergraph attains the squared-degree extremum; proof, refutation, or a sufficient quantitative relaxation remains open.

formal_statement.body: $$k>\frac N2,\quad m=\binom Ak,\quad A\ge k\quad\Longrightarrow\quad D^2_{N,k}(m)=D^2(K_{A,k}),$$

scope.domain: Extremal combinatorics of uniform hypergraphs concerning sums of squared vertex degrees.
assumptions: m equals the number of k-subsets of an A-element set
parameters: N: parameter indexing the extremal quantity
A: number of vertices supporting the complete k-uniform hypergraph
scope.unresolved_remainder: Resolve Conjecture 1 by proving or refuting it, or establish a quantitatively relaxed version sufficient for the memory-bounded switching lemma.

citations.label: Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption

progress.summary: The paper explicitly presents this as Conjecture 1 among important questions left open. It states that resolving the conjecture, or a relaxed version sufficient for its final statement, remains necessary.
citation_labels: Joseph Jaeger et al., Tight Time-Memory Trade-Offs for Symmetric Encryption
